q: A customer contacted a vacation rental host about trouble entering. The host came to help within 10 minutes. What service quality dimension is demonstrated?
explanation: Quick response = Responsiveness. Assurance = knowledge/courtesy. Reliability = consistent delivery. Tangibles = physical appearance.

q: A service center employee was polite, professional, explained tire options clearly, and answered all questions. What service quality dimension?
explanation: Knowledgeable + polite + professional = Assurance (inspiring trust/confidence). Not Responsiveness (speed).

q: A hotel manager periodically inspects rooms to assess condition. Which cost of quality?
explanation: Inspecting/checking quality = Appraisal. Prevention = stopping defects before they happen. Appraisal = catching them after production.

q: A utility website makes customers enter bank info twice and compares data before proceeding. Which cost of quality?
explanation: System designed to PREVENT errors before they occur = Prevention costs. Not appraisal (that's checking after the fact).

q: A business sends surveys asking which features customers like and want added. Which TQM principle?
explanation: Surveying customers about preferences = Customer-centered focus. Continuous improvement = ongoing process changes.

q: A manufacturer collaborates with a component supplier to customize parts for optimal quality. Which TQM concept?
explanation: Working closely with suppliers to customize components = Supplier relationships.

q: Which activity is in the Define phase of Six Sigma?
explanation: DMAIC: Define = detail the problem/opportunity. Measure = assess current. Analyze = identify causes. Improve = train/implement. Control = sustain.

q: Which Six Sigma phase implements measures to make errors more quickly detectable?
explanation: Control phase = monitoring systems to sustain improvements and detect errors quickly. Last step of DMAIC.

q: A manager wants to see how many tools had RPM in specific ranges (10000-10049, 10050-10099, etc). Which quality tool?
explanation: Frequency distribution across ranges = Histogram. Scatterplot = relationship between two variables. Check sheet = data collection form.

q: A manager wants to see if number of defects is related to total units produced per day. Which tool?
explanation: Relationship between two variables = Scatterplot. Control chart = process stability over time. Pareto = 80/20 ranking.

q: What is a factor accounted for in effective capacity?
explanation: Effective capacity = design capacity minus PLANNED reductions (breaks, maintenance). Unplanned outages reduce ACTUAL output, not effective capacity.

q: Design capacity 40,000 shirts/mo. Effective capacity 31,000. Actual output 24,180. What is efficiency?
explanation: Efficiency = Actual/Effective = 24,180/31,000 = 0.78 = 78%. Utilization would be Actual/Design = 24,180/40,000 = 60.45%.

q: Which scenario demonstrates a resource constraint?
choices: Shortage of raw materials hindering production
Overabundance of inventory from slow sales
Running out of storage for finished products
explanation: Resource constraint = not enough of a needed resource. Raw material shortage = resource constraint. Machine bottleneck = process constraint.

q: After dedicating resources to eliminate a constraint in TOC, what is the next step?
choices: Evaluate whether system has another constraint
Make constraint known to all departments
explanation: TOC: Identify > Exploit > Subordinate > Elevate (dedicate resources) > REPEAT (go back, check for new constraint). It's a cycle.

q: Company wants to hold very little inventory by aligning capacity with demand closely. Which strategy?
explanation: Match = adjust capacity to match demand. Lead = build capacity before demand. Lag = add capacity after demand exceeds current.

q: Which is an example of lead capacity strategy?
choices: Increased production based on detailed forecasts
Increased output after jackets sold out for months
Reduced production after inventory maxed out
Significantly increases production in anticipation of high demand
explanation: Lead = increase capacity BEFORE demand arrives, based on anticipation. Option A is forecast-based (could be match). D is clearly anticipatory = Lead.

q: Products with very little variation and interchangeable parts. Which production process?
explanation: Low variation + interchangeable parts = Assembly line. Job shop = high variety/low volume. Continuous flow = single product, never stops (chemicals, oil).

q: Manufacturer produces four boat models, one model per week. Which facility layout?
explanation: Producing one product type at a time in sequence = Product layout. Process layout = grouped by function (all drills together, all saws together).

q: Fast food restaurant opening second location. Major factor in location decision?
explanation: Fast food = service business = customers come to you. Proximity to customers is #1. Manufacturing would prioritize transportation/materials.

q: Software company needs new office location. Major consideration?
explanation: Software company needs talent. Quality community = good labor pool, amenities, lifestyle that attracts skilled workers.

q: Facility needs to minimize costs, improve margins, achieve economies of scale. What to do?
explanation: Economies of scale = high volume of SAME thing. Reduce variation = more standardization = more scale efficiency.

q: Business produces single product, wants economies of scale in new facility. Which processes?
explanation: Single product + economies of scale = Assembly line. Job shop = custom/varied work. Project = one-offs.

q: Which forecasting step assesses accuracy of the initial method?
explanation: Developing and testing = build the model then TEST its accuracy. Applying = using it for real. Constraints = real-world limits.

q: Which forecasting step accounts for real-world limitations?
explanation: Considering constraints = accounting for real-world limitations (budget, data availability, time). Straight definition match.

q: Which planning component is part of short-range planning?
explanation: Short-range = Master Production Schedule (weeks/days). Medium = Aggregate plan. Long-range = Strategic plan.

q: Company sells phones plus replacement screens, batteries, cables. Which is dependent demand?
explanation: Dependent demand = items needed BECAUSE of another item (parts inside the phone). Speaker is built into the phone, not sold separately. Screens/batteries/cables are sold independently.

q: Executive wants objective, mathematical forecasting model. Which model?
explanation: Quantitative/mathematical = Weighted moving average. Survey, Delphi, Pyramid are all qualitative (human judgment).

q: Manager creates forecast by starting at the bottom and adding component parts. Which method?
explanation: Bottom-up aggregation = Pyramid method. Exponential smoothing and moving average are quantitative, not bottom-up qualitative.

q: Scheduling that determines demand in advance while limiting access to the service?
explanation: Reservations = know demand ahead of time + limit capacity access. Hotels, restaurants, airlines all use this.

q: Fast-food kiosks where patrons place their own orders. Which scheduling technique?
explanation: Customers doing the work themselves = Consumer self-service. Reduces labor needs.

q: Organization implementing software to manage and integrate core processes. Which role?
explanation: ERP integrates core processes = improves collaboration across departments. Call scripts = CRM. Supplier contracts = SCM.

q: ERP generates invoice and updates inventory when client orders. Which functionality?
explanation: Automatic invoice + inventory update triggered by order = Processing and automation. Integration = connecting systems.

q: Rearranging machinery to reduce unnecessary worker movements. Benefit?
explanation: Reducing unnecessary movements = eliminating waste = improved efficiency. One of the 8 wastes in lean (Motion).

q: Production manager asks for improvement ideas monthly. Which lean benefit?
explanation: Soliciting ideas from employees = involving them in improvement = Enhanced employee engagement. Core lean principle.

q: Which scenario is a non-value-added activity?
choices: Grocery associate counting inventory all day
explanation: Counting inventory adds zero value to the product. Assembly, cooking, examining = directly creating or delivering value.

q: Which competitive advantage is associated with lean systems?
explanation: Lean = eliminate waste. Inventory is a form of waste. Inventory reduction is THE hallmark lean advantage.

q: Benefit of reducing inventory through lean principles?
explanation: Less inventory = less time sitting idle (not being used/sold). B is wrong (lean reduces, doesn't eliminate). D is wrong (less inventory INCREASES stockout risk).

q: What is a benefit of TQM?
explanation: TQM reduces defects = fewer products need warranty repairs. Quality up = rework down.

q: How is flexibility enhanced through lean strategies?
explanation: Eliminating waste movements frees capacity and allows workers to adapt. Specialization REDUCES flexibility. More inventory isn't lean.

q: Production facility uses small lots and low inventory. What signals need for more materials?
explanation: Kanban = visual signal card that triggers replenishment in a pull system. Heijunka = production leveling. Kanban is THE lean signal system.

q: Food facility has long setup times on primary machine. How to improve?
explanation: SMED (Single Minute Exchange): make tools/dies readily available to reduce setup time. Having to search for tools wastes time.

q: Facility produces several products. Manager wants lean production efficiency. Which strategy?
choices: Match component production to final assembly schedule
Large batches of one product before switching
explanation: Lean = pull system, match production to demand/assembly. Push systems, large batches, and high inventory are all anti-lean.

q: Silicon imports blocked by sanctions. Which bottleneck type?
explanation: Sanctions = government regulation blocking supply = Regulatory bottleneck.

q: Software company slowed by lack of skilled workers for customization. Bottleneck type?
explanation: Not enough skilled workers = Labor bottleneck. Physical = space/infrastructure. Financial = money.

q: Cheese factory system processes only 6 boxes/min causing truck delays. Bottleneck category?
explanation: Slow scanning system = Technology bottleneck. The system's processing speed is the limit, not physical space.

q: Facility manager must sign off on inspections but is busy with admin. Shipments delayed. Bottleneck?
explanation: One person's approval required but unavailable = Decision-making bottleneck. Not regulatory (it's internal policy, not law).

q: Logging company limited by single-lane forest road despite high demand. Bottleneck?
explanation: Single-lane road = physical infrastructure constraint = Physical bottleneck.

q: Guitar manufacturer can't pay suppliers due to cashflow issues. Bottleneck?
explanation: Can't pay suppliers = not enough cash = Financial bottleneck.

q: Retail company buys a distribution center to lower costs. Which strategy?
explanation: Retailer buying distribution (upstream toward supplier) = Backward vertical integration. Moving backward in the supply chain.

q: Fabric producer buys the distribution center that buys most of its fabric. Which strategy?
explanation: Producer buying distributor (downstream toward customer) = Forward vertical integration. Moving forward in the supply chain.

q: Fashion company needs innovation, works only with suppliers who adjust quickly. Which strategy?
explanation: Frequent change + quick adjustment = Agile supply chain. Lean = stable demand, waste elimination. Agile = volatile demand, flexibility.

q: Furniture company, high volume/low variety, suppliers committed to eliminating waste. Strategy?
explanation: High volume + low variety + eliminate waste + minimize costs = Lean supply chain. Classic lean profile.

q: Fencing company, low margins, works with suppliers to minimize costs. Which concept?
explanation: Low margins + minimize costs + close supplier collaboration = Lean supply chain.

q: Lumber supplier monitors furniture manufacturer's stock and delivers when needed. Strategy?
explanation: Supplier monitors and replenishes customer's inventory = VMI (Vendor Managed Inventory). Supplier takes ownership of inventory management.

q: New ops manager wants ethical operations. What is directly their responsibility?
explanation: Operations manager = production/manufacturing. Environmental pollution from operations is directly their responsibility. Pricing = marketing. Accounting = finance.

q: Operations manager wants higher emphasis on ethics. Important consideration?
explanation: Product safety = ethical obligation of operations. Defective products harm customers. Inventory method and design are operational, not primarily ethical.

q: Company leaders want to emphasize social sustainability. What should they do?
explanation: Social sustainability = people. Job security = taking care of employees = social. Long-term savings = economic. Collaboration = operational.

q: Organization redesigning operations for environmental sustainability. Which action?
explanation: Environmental sustainability = reducing resource depletion. Respect/dignity = social sustainability.

q: Organization gives all employees four mental health personal days. Which triple bottom line component?
explanation: Mental health days for employees = caring for people = Social responsibility. Triple bottom line: People, Planet, Profit.

q: What is a benefit of SWOT analysis?
choices: Defines how to compete in market
explanation: SWOT helps identify and capitalize on opportunities while mitigating threats. That's its core purpose.

q: What is a primary consideration of SWOT analysis?
explanation: External threats (elements that could create difficulties) are one of the four primary SWOT considerations.

q: Which question should a company ask when determining SWOT opportunities?
choices: Which competitors have greatest customer base?
What do advantageous external changes look like?
explanation: Opportunities = advantageous EXTERNAL changes. Internal = strengths/weaknesses. External = opportunities/threats.

q: Which factor represents a source of opportunities in SWOT?
explanation: Government policy change = EXTERNAL factor = opportunity (or threat). Management, competencies, QC are all internal.

q: What is one of the two internal elements of SWOT?
explanation: Internal = Strengths + Weaknesses. External = Opportunities + Threats. SW are internal, OT are external.

q: Clothing retailer uses perpetual inventory. What is an advantage?
explanation: Perpetual = always know what you have (real-time tracking). That's its #1 advantage.

q: Manufacturing facility uses perpetual system. What is a disadvantage?
explanation: Perpetual systems need technology, software, scanners = expensive to maintain. That's the tradeoff for real-time data.

q: Small grocery uses periodic inventory. Which advantage?
explanation: Periodic = manual counts at intervals. Advantage: simple, no computer needed. Disadvantage: don't know exact levels between counts.

q: Auto parts retailer uses periodic system. Which drawback?
explanation: Periodic = only know inventory at count time. Between counts, exact balances are unknown. That's the core drawback.

q: Which model assumes manufacturing capacity exceeds demand?
explanation: EPQ (Economic Production Quantity) = you make it yourself, production rate > demand rate. EOQ = you buy it from someone else.

q: Which costs are primarily considered in inventory management models?
explanation: Three primary inventory costs: ordering, carrying/holding, and STOCKOUT. Insurance is a subset of carrying. Sunk/selling aren't inventory model costs.

q: Which inventory cost includes costs of lost customers?
explanation: Stockout = running out of stock = lost sales + lost customers + backorder costs. Carrying = storage, insurance, obsolescence.

q: What is an inventory level that triggers the replenishment process?
explanation: Order point (reorder point) = when inventory hits this level, place a new order. Safety stock = buffer. Lead time = delivery wait time.
